# Clinical Lab Operations Analysis (SQL)

**Goal:** analyze 20,000 lab orders (Jul–Sep 2026) to find where turnaround time (TAT) and reagent waste can be improved.
**Tool:** SQL (SQLite). **Data:** synthetic, generated by `build_db.py`. No real patient data.

## Data model
`orders` (20,000 rows) -> `tests`, `analyzers` (7), `patients` (2,000; wards: ICU, CCU, Operations, OPD, Ward)

## SQL skills covered (12 queries in `queries.sql`)
JOIN (up to 3 tables), GROUP BY / HAVING, CASE WHEN, CTEs, window functions (RANK, LAG, NTILE, running SUM), date math, self-join.

## Key findings
1. Potassium (target 30 min) misses its TAT target in ~78% of orders, the worst of all tests.
2. Chem-B and Hema-B repeat ~8% of tests vs ~4% on their A twins: double the reagent waste.
3. B analyzers are also 6-9 minutes slower per test than the A analyzers in the same section.
4. Workload peaks in the morning shift (~65% of orders).

## Recommendation
Review calibration/QC on Chem-B and Hema-B, and route STAT potassium to Chem-A.

## How to run
`sqlite3 lab.db < queries.sql`  (or open lab.db in DB Browser for SQLite)
